transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been troubling you or what brings you here today?

I came in because I just can’t stop noticing this sagging, uneven area around my jaw and neck. I know people tell me it looks normal, but it doesn’t feel normal to me. When families come in, or nurses, or people at church look at me, I feel like that’s the first thing they see.
Do you find yourself doing anything repeatedly, like checking mirrors, touching the area, or trying to cover it up, because you’re so focused on how it looks?

Yes. Before I leave for work or for a meeting, I keep going back to the bathroom mirror and checking it. I’ll fix my collar, move my hair around my neck, then look again in my phone camera. Sometimes I ask my daughter if it looks strange. It’s gotten me late more than once.
Can you describe what exactly you see in the mirror that concerns you? Do you think it’s an imagined or slight change, or do you believe it’s a significant defect that others should also notice?

I see this sagging spot around my jaw and down into my neck, like it’s uneven compared to the other side. To me it looks very obvious, even though people keep saying it looks normal. I don’t know if other people truly notice it the way I do, but it feels like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church see when they look at me.
Have you ever considered that others may not notice this sagging area as much as you do, or do you believe they are just being polite when they say it looks normal?

I’ve thought about that, yes. I know people tell me it looks normal, and maybe they don’t see it the way I do. But it’s hard for me to believe it, because I can’t stop seeing that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. When someone looks at me, I feel like that’s the first thing they notice, even if they’re just being polite and not saying anything.

Does this concern about the sagging area on your jaw and neck cause you a lot of distress, or has it affected your daily life, such as avoiding social situations or spending a lot of time focused on your appearance?

Yes, it does. I’ve turned down chances to lead meetings or take on more supervisory parts at work because I’m worried everyone will be looking at my face and neck. And I get stuck trying to make myself look okay before I leave, so then I fall behind on paperwork.

I’ve also stopped going to some of my book club and walking club things. Getting ready just feels like too much sometimes, and I don’t want people staring at it.
Have you noticed that your mood is affected most of the time, like feeling down, losing interest in things you used to enjoy, or having trouble sleeping or eating?

I’m not really sure. I mean, I do get upset and frustrated about how I look, but I haven’t really paid attention to whether my mood is down most of the time. Sleep and eating… I don’t know, I haven’t noticed anything clear there.
Do you feel anxious or fearful about people noticing the sagging area, and does this feeling interfere with your ability to function in social or work settings?

Yes. I get really anxious that people are going to notice my face and neck. At work I’ve passed up chances to help lead meetings or do more supervisory things because I’m worried everyone will be looking at it. And sometimes I spend so long trying to make myself look presentable that I end up falling behind on paperwork.

Socially, too, I’ve stopped going to some of my book club and walking club activities because getting ready feels like too much, and I don’t want to be around people when I feel like that.
Do you find yourself thinking about this sagging area for hours each day, even when you're trying to focus on other things?

Yes. It’s on my mind a lot during the day. I’ll be trying to focus on work or talking to someone, and I still keep thinking about that sagging, uneven spot around my jaw and neck. Even when people tell me it looks normal, I feel like it’s the first thing families, nurses, or people at church notice when they look at me.

Is your main concern about how your jaw and neck look, such as the sagging and unevenness, or is it more about feeling embarrassed or self-conscious that others are judging your appearance in social situations?

It’s mainly about how it looks to me—the sagging and unevenness around my jaw and neck. I just can’t stop seeing it. And even when people say it looks normal, I still feel like it’s the first thing people notice when they look at me, whether it’s families, nurses, or people at church.
